name: Whitestone Hill Campground
note: Primitive camping on a mown lawn in the north-west corner of the Whitestone Hill State Historic Site grounds, across the lake from the battlefield memorial; the grounds fill for a powwow once each summer. The State Historical Society's page does not mention camping, so call the site before setting out. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: 2026-11-12, public-campground ladder step 3: Google Maps place 'Whitestone Hill Campground' (category Campground, 'Located in: Whitestone Hill State Historic Site', website history.nd.gov, no phone, 46.16970,-98.86171), whose one review (Local Guide, 'a year ago') describes camping several nights there with '1 vault toilet in the campground', grills and picnic tables; The Dyrt 'Whitestone Hill Historic Site' (46.17001,-98.86163) has three dated camping reviews (May 2024 'big wide open space... park anywhere', July 2024 'quiet place to spend the night', June 2025). Operator: State Historical Society of North Dakota (SHSND page history.nd.gov/historicsites/whitestone: 7310 86th St SE, open year round, free admission, picnic area with shelter, table, pit toilets and parking lot; it does not mention camping). Steps 1-2 fail: no SHSND page or document names the camping, and ndtourism (two titles, 'Whitestone Hill Lake Campground' and 'Whitestone Hill State Historic Site Campground') refuses and is never a source. Treated as a designated agency camping area, not dispersed, because Google files it as a campground inside the historic site with its own toilet and tables (precedent: Fort Buford SHS 5891, state, 'no numbered sites'). Not on the ND HHS licensed list 07.17.2025 (Dickey County: only Huebner Trailer Park and Trinity Bible College; no SHSND rows anywhere on the list). Not on RV Life (Algolia, 15 km radius) or Campendium; not on the Dickey County Park Board page (county parks are Wilson Dam and Pheasant Lake only). Esri imagery: gravel section-line roads to an open mown lawn west of a grass track, with a small toilet building and a table/grill structure at the tree edge; no pads or pedestals, so rig fit rests on open ground (no length limit, 4WD or road wording anywhere; The Dyrt tags it big-rig friendly). No horse facilities mentioned. No DB entry within 5 km (nearest Wilson Dam 15678 at 8.3 km).
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-12: Esri World Imagery at 900 m, 300 m and z19 frames around 46.1700,-98.8620 (all rendered). The lake (~15-20 ha, the historic site's lake; SHSND 'a freshwater lake') lies south-east. The identifiable camping area (Google pin, toilet and table structure) is the mown lawn north of a dense tree belt; open water is ~80-90 m away, through that tree belt and a cattail fringe to the west bay, or across marshy grass to the north-west cove. The lawn's east end, past the grass track, comes within ~50-60 m of the cove over open grass, but nothing places camping there (no pads, no sites, and the circular tracks there may be powwow parking). No site proven on or overlooking the water -> default down to not waterfront. Dam check: no NID dam near; Open-Meteo DEM 607 m at the lawn vs 603 m on the lake, so the camping is above the water, not below any berm.
fees_source: The Dyrt 'Whitestone Hill Historic Site' listing ('FREE established camping', read 2026-11-12) and the SHSND site page ('Free admission, donations welcome', read 2026-11-12); no fee or pay station named by any source or reviewer

sites.note: No numbered sites or pads: open mown lawn, park anywhere.

sites_source: The Dyrt reviews (Teresa T., May 2024: 'a big wide open space that I'm sure you can park anywhere you want'; listing: no formal sites, open grass area), read 2026-11-12; Esri imagery 2026-11-12 shows no pads
facilities_source: Google Maps 'Whitestone Hill Campground' review ('1 vault toilet in the campground'), read 2026-11-12; SHSND page (picnic area with 'pit toilets'), read 2026-11-12
season_source: https://www.history.nd.gov/historicsites/whitestone/ ('Open year round'; 'there is no snow removal service'), read 2026-11-12; the Google reviewer mentions winter camping
booking_source: The Dyrt listing (first come, first served), read 2026-11-12; no booking channel on the SHSND page or anywhere else
curation_note: ND lead 20 (2026-11-12): added on Google Maps 'Whitestone Hill Campground' (inside the SHSND historic site) plus Google and The Dyrt camping reviews 2024-2025; the SHSND page itself never mentions camping. ndtourism search snippets claim electricity (one title says 3 electrical hookups and no water or dump, the other 10 RV sites with electric); unreadable and contradicted by reviewers ('no services' beyond a restroom and tables), so hookups were left unknown. --Claude
flags: Thin agency evidence: kept on public-ladder step 3 (Google lists it as a campground inside the historic site; a review from about a year ago and The Dyrt reviews May 2024 - June 2025 confirm camping). SHSND's own page does not mention camping. If AWH reads it as a dispersed allowance needing an agency designation (Homestake Pass 6071 rule), it would be a skip.
Hookups left unknown: ndtourism snippets say 3 (or 10) electric sites, reviewers say no services; imagery too coarse for pedestals.
Fees $0 rests on The Dyrt's 'FREE' tag and SHSND free admission; no source names a camping fee.
Waterfront: lakeview possible if campers use the lawn's east end (~50-60 m over open grass to the lake's north-west cove); nothing places camping there, so default down.
Name: Google's 'Whitestone Hill Campground' used rather than the ndtourism titles ('Whitestone Hill Lake Campground' / 'Whitestone Hill State Historic Site Campground').

Phone list: Whitestone Hill State Historic Site / SHSND, 701-328-3508 (SHSND main 701-328-2666): is overnight camping allowed on the north-west lawn, are there any electric hookups (how many), is there a fee, and is drinking water available?
